summary: samantha-health-manager.sh now supervises core-services-watchdog.sh --gateway-only through its existing check_supervisor (same family as the adb and remote-desktop watchdogs). In that mode the watchdog never starts the Companion and acts on the Gateway only while no Companion process exists, always under the existing repair lease; its singleton lock is now actually held. The supervisor pattern is anchored so that test-core-services-watchdog.sh never counts as the supervisor nor gets stopped as stale.
reason: S24 01/11 (read only): core-services-watchdog.sh, hardened by #506, had no owner (no process, last log 2026-10-07, nothing in Termux:Boot, Tier0, the root guardian or the health manager). A Gateway alive but silent while the Companion is stopped was restarted by nobody. Launching the watchdog as it was would also have doubled the Companion supervision (heal cp restarts the Companion outside the lease, against the health manager check_http) and the Gateway supervision (heal gw starts the Gateway without the lease while the Companion watchdog does the same).

tests.name: installer/termux-lite/test-health-gateway-fallback-owner.py
tests.evidence: Real health-manager functions drive the real watchdog as a real process in an isolated HOME: absent = started once with --gateway-only; three further passes = still one process, state healthy, one restart attempt; a second manual copy exits on the held singleton lock; a legacy instance without the option is replaced (stale_runtime, budget exempt); AI gate unavailable with no Companion process = direct bounded start (budget 1/3); AI gate unavailable with a Companion = no start; a running test-core-services-watchdog.sh (CI or a localci-s24 diagnostic) is neither counted as the supervisor nor stopped as stale (anchored pattern); static checks: single owner in the main loop, no other launcher (guardian, Tier0 bootstrap, boot scripts, other watchdogs) starts it, the Companion keeps check_http as its only health-manager starter. Registered in .github/workflows/ci.yml.

tests.name: installer/termux-lite/test-core-services-watchdog.sh
tests.evidence: Cases 1-9 of #506 unchanged and green. New --gateway-only cases with real processes: Companion alive = nothing, lease never taken, owner hand-off logged once; Companion absent and silent Gateway = exact PID stopped and restarted under the lease, relaunched Gateway detached and holding neither the lease nor the singleton lock; Companion and Gateway absent = one start under the lease; health-manager repair lease held = deferred; a Companion appearing while the lease is taken = no start; gateway-start.sh still preparing = no second start; singleton held for the life of the loop and released at exit; unknown option refused (64); the Companion is never started.

capabilities.reason: Internal supervision only; no route, setting or app action.

architecture.reason: Existing owner (health manager check_supervisor) launches an existing script; same repair lease, restart budget and AI admission. No new supervisor, daemon, store, scheduler or retry engine.

evidence: Health-manager supervision of the core-services watchdog only.

limitations: Full canonical CI on the final GitHub head remains required.
The S24 still runs the pre-#506 watchdog in its release (361df3ff line); the owner and the hardened watchdog take effect together at the next companion-deploy.sh.

While a Companion process lives, the Gateway relies on the Companion watchdog alone (unchanged): a live Companion with its listener watchdog disabled (CLAWMOBILE_WHATSAPP_LISTENER_WATCHDOG=0, unset on the S24) is not covered here.
With a Companion present, a missing watchdog is restarted only through the AI admission like the other supervisors; the direct start applies only when no Companion process exists.
health-verdict.py publishes no immune.core_services_watchdog capability (the watchdog writes no heartbeat); the health manager state and log carry its status.
rollback: Revert this commit and redeploy the core with companion-deploy.sh; the health manager then stops supervising the watchdog, and a running instance can be stopped by its PID.
